title: The MESAS Project: ALMA Observations of the F-type Stars γ Lep, γ Vir A, and γ Vir B
question: What are the submm/mm fluxes and chromospheric structure of debris-poor F-type stars, and is there short-term variability or bias for debris disk studies?

data.sensitivity: gamma Lep 30 (B7), 10 (B6) uJy/beam; gamma Vir 15 (B7), 10 (B6) uJy/beam

what.value: Solar semi-empirical model used as starting atmosphere

evidence.quote: a semi-empirical Solar model (cite: avrett) in hydrostatic equilibrium was adopted as the starting point

what.value: Stellar parameters (distance, radius, Teff) in Table

external_data.citation: footnotes a-e not given in text

recipe.method: CLEAN with natural weighting, threshold 1/2 sigma_rms
Point-source uvmodelfit to visibilities per EB
assumptions: Stars are point sources; absolute flux uncertainty ~10%

recipe.goal: Characterize background source near gamma Vir
recipe.method: Point and Gaussian uvmodelfit; Gaussian preferred; spectral index and beta from two bands
KINICH-PAKAL iteratively modifies temperature/density profiles, ionization and opacity of a solar base model to fit ALMA and Herschel data
assumptions: Non-LTE ionization-excitation and radiative transfer; hydrostatic equilibrium Avrett & Loeser solar starting model

recipe.method: uvmodelfit applied to each on-source scan (6-8 min between phase calibrations); compare stars with background source

recipe.goal: Estimate debris excess and mass for gamma Vir B
recipe.method: Compare Band 6 flux with Sirius-like (~0.6 TB) and full-blackbody extrapolations; debris masses per White et al. 2017
key_parameters: ring at 4 au; grain density 2.5 g cm^-3; 2-4 au disk, 10 um to 25 km, q~3.5

answer_key.quantity: gamma Vir B flux 1.29 mm (2019 Mar 18)

evidence.quote: The Band 7 total flux is $430\pm25~\mu \rm Jy$ and the Band 6 total flux is $160\pm16~\mu \rm Jy$.

we see a temperature minimum of T$_{R, min}$ = 4800 K (T$_{eff}$/T$_{R, min}$ = 0.76) at a height of 750 km above the photosphere

answer_key.quantity: Debris excess for gamma Vir B (Sirius-like / blackbody)

evidence.quote: we would get an excess of 180 $\mu$Jy and 65 $\mu$Jy, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Total debris mass in disk (size distribution)

evidence.quote: This would lead us to infer $0.02-0.07\,\rm M_{\oplus}$ of total debris in the disk

Whether pipeline products were used or manually re-imaged; spectral line flagging

score_reason: Flux measurement is easily repeatable with archival data, but atmospheric modeling and variability analysis lack details.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from ALMA cycle 5/6 projects likely public, and fluxes via uvmodelfit are numeric and reproducible.
